extraction.name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
extraction.description: A benchmark to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated by appending verifiable instructions to base prompts, filtering illogical ones via few-shot prompting, rephrasing for diversity, and finally manually checking and editing them.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts generated with randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to them.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Few-shot prompting was used to rephrase each prompt to increase the diversity of phrasing.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Illogical prompts were identified and removed using few-shot prompting.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to improve the prompts and verifiable instructions to make them more related to real-world applications and expand the approach with more instructions and multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Ensuring LLMs can consistently adhere to given directives is paramount for safety and reliability, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically, leading to edge cases. Strict string matching can yield false negatives, while loose verification criteria can introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models.

name.evidence: we introduce Instruction-Following Eval ( IFEval ) for large language models.

description.evidence: We propose IFEval: Instruction-Following Eval, a benchmark to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions.

url.evidence: Our code and data can be found at https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/instruction_following_eval

creator.evidence: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou

rai:dataCollection.evidence: First, we generate a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt. Then, we use few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and remove them. As the third step, we apply another few-shot prompting based approach to rephrase each prompt, to increase the diversity of phrasing. Finally, we manually check and edit the rephrased prompts one by one.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we apply another few-shot prompting based approach to rephrase each prompt... Finally, we manually check and edit the rephrased prompts one by one.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: First, we generate a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: As the third step, we apply another few-shot prompting based approach to rephrase each prompt, to increase the diversity of phrasing.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Then, we use few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and remove them.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: As part of our future work, we plan to improve the prompts and verifiable instructions, to make them more related to real-world applications. In addition, we plan to expand our approach with more verifiable instructions, and the support of multi-modal use cases.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The capability of LLMs to accurately interpret and follow natural language instructions is crucial, not only for the precision of tasks but also for the safety and reliability of their implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically – there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed... Although this loose instruction-following verification process reduces false negatives, it is likely to introduce false positives.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We propose IFEval: Instruction-Following Eval, a benchmark to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions.
